background: Son of Hall of Fame coach Rick Adelman. Coached Oregon high-school ball (Jesuit, Lincoln) before joining the Timberwolves in player development/assistant roles (2011-16) under his father and Flip Saunders, then one season under Frank Vogel in Orlando (2016-17). Joined Michael Malone's Denver staff in 2017, rising to lead assistant/offensive coordinator and winning the 2023 title; widely credited with Denver's Jokic-centric set design and ATO plays. Named interim coach on April 8, 2025 when Malone was fired with three games left, went 3-0, beat the Clippers in seven and pushed eventual champion Oklahoma City to seven games, and was named the 17th head coach in franchise history on May 22, 2025. Led Denver to 54-28 (3rd in the West) and the league's top offense for much of 2025-26 despite major injuries, but was upset 2-4 in the first round by a depleted Minnesota team. Defense is delegated to coordinator Jared Dudley; Adelman has described wanting fewer transition-dependent possessions and more called sets, and has not been shy about zone.

research_notes: Records for 2024-25 (3-0 interim; team 50-32) and 2025-26 (54-28, lost R1 2-4 to MIN) are well sourced. 2026 R1 Games 4 and 5 results were not individually confirmed; the 2-4 series total follows from Game 6 being the clincher with Denver having won Game 1 and the Wolves Games 2, 3 and 6, so Denver must have won exactly one of Games 4/5. 2026-27 record through 2026-11-02 not verified (shared web-search budget was exhausted); one aggregator showed 1-2. No tracking data found on pace, 3PA rate, drop-vs-switch frequency, challenge success, two-for-one or foul-up-three behavior; those scores are estimates. Age 45 assumes a May 1981 birth date. One search result erroneously described Adelman as deceased in 2018; disregarded as a mis-attributed record.
